notes.omp.db.rows: Rows in ~/.omp/agent/skill-descriptions.db are keyed by sha256(template | 0x00 | name | 0x00 | description-as-loaded) and are never pruned, so the count grows whenever the host ever offers a new (name, description) pair — including a project-scoped copy of a skill the user root also carries (round 13: a ufo copy under ~/Projects/origin-work/ufo-fsd-alpha). The equal pin is a change detector: a move means 're-record deliberately, naming the mechanism', not 'the live catalogue changed'. keys_reproduced and verified_skills are the invariants.
notes.omp.offered.dangling: recorded dangling entries: sekhmet, xbrd in ~/.agents/skills (symlinks into a vanished port). Relinking or deleting them changes this count - a deliberate baseline move, not drift.
notes.omp.elf.template_sha256: sha256 of the 273-byte compression prompt embedded in the omp ELF; a new omp build or a prompt edit moves it, which invalidates every cache key.
notes.oc.log.init_count_max: max of `message=init count=N`; opencode logs only counts, never name sets.
notes.oc.dup.existing_claude/oc.dup.duplicate_: both must stay > 0 - that is the evidence for last-parsed-wins under unbounded discovery concurrency.
notes.omp.catalogue.matched: newest captured <skills> block; every line must byte-equal that skill's cached description (the freeze means a lagging block is the signal, not noise)
